布列塔尼轟炸管起源於中世紀伊比利亞半島，後傳入法國西北部的布列塔尼地區。這種雙簧: The Breton bombarde originated in the Iberian peninsula in the Middle Ages and later spread to Brittany in north-western France. This double-reed woodwind took its finished form over the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and is known for its powerful, penetrating timbre. The bombarde was at first used for religious ceremony and military occasions, and takes its name from its loud voice. As Breton folk culture developed, the instrument became an important part of local traditional music, playing a leading role in particular in folk festivals and in bagad pipe bands. From the nineteenth century to the present the bombarde has served as a symbol of Breton identity, continuing to play a part in traditional performance and finding new life in the folk revival; it has become a model for the preservation and transmission of traditional European instruments.
